Missed Connection – Flash nightclub Saturday at 300am

By Prince Of Petworth
Published November 16, 2026 at 3:00PM

photo by Beau Finley

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 0:56
Instaread

Ed. Note: If this was you and you are interested, please email princeofpetworth@gmail.com so I can put you in touch with OP.

“Dear PoPville,

Absolute stunner of a lady going into Flash nightclub Saturday at 300am, as I was waiting outside for an Uber. I was clearly and perhaps awkwardly admiring her beauty, when she noticed. We exchanged smiles and she said “Hiiii” as she entered the club. She had curly dark hair and a beautiful smile. I was in a denim jacket and had on a black beanie with white lettering. She, perhaps, was from out of town or it was her first time at Flash, as she said: “Is this Flash” to her friend before entering. Shot in the dark, but can’t let this one go without at least trying to connect, or at minimum give her figurative flowers.”

Ed. Note: If this is you, please email princeofpetworth@gmail.com so I can put you in touch with OP. PoPville is not affiliated with either party, please proceed with any potential connection at your own risk using caution as you would any online encounter. For those curious about past missed connections, many have been made and when possible I’ll try to update when/if more are made. Last week’s monkey wrench/REI MC was connected!

“Help Susan Heal After the Logan Circle Shooting”

By Prince Of Petworth
Published November 16, 2026 at 2:15PM

“Dear PoPville,

Got this from a friend who’s connected to the family. The woman who was in critical condition following Thursday’s shooting was just here to dog sit for her daughter and got caught up in the foray in the most tragic way possible.”

The GoFundMe says:

“On the morning of November 12, my mom, Susan Thurston Hamerski, was walking our mini-golden doodle, Wrigley, near our apartment in Washington, D.C.’s Logan Circle neighborhood when she was shot in a mass shooting. She was struck in the face.

Thanks to the brilliant work of her trauma team in D.C., Mom is now in stable condition. But her road ahead will be long and hard. She faces multiple surgeries to restore function to her jaw and tongue, reconstructive surgery to repair her face, and months of rehabilitative therapy.

Mom was in D.C. for the happiest of reasons: my wedding. When my husband and I left on our honeymoon, she stayed behind to take care of Wrigley for us. That’s who she is. We cut our honeymoon short to be by her side. (Wrigley is safe and back home.)

Back home in Minnesota, so many people know Mom’s generosity: her work at the Minnesota Department of Health, her service on the Illusion Theater board, and her award-winning writing and poetry. For six years she served as social media lead for the local Moms Demand Action, sharing gun-safety news and research with her community. Even in the ICU, her thoughts turned to others. From her hospital bed, she wrote: “Gun control is a public health crisis.”

The costs are enormous and will continue for months, both in D.C. and back home in the Twin Cities. We don’t yet know when she’ll be able to work again.

A post from The Montgomery County Economic Development Corporation

MCEDC President & CEO Jared Smith Named to the Washington Business Journal’s Power 250 List

Published October 28, 2026 at 12:45PM

Last week, MCEDC President & CEO Jared Smith and other local Montgomery County business leaders were named to the Washington Business Journal’s Power 250 List, which recognizes influential business leaders across the DMV region. Smith, who joined MCEDC in December 2025, brings over 20 years of economic development and business experience across local and state government to the role. He is widely recognized in the economic development field and chairs the International Economic Development Council’s national Committee on the Future of the Profession, helping shape strategies that influence communities across the U.S.

During his time at MCEDC, Smith has led the development of the new Countywide Economic Development Strategic Plan for Montgomery County. The strategic plan establishes a clear, actionable framework to guide economic growth, competitiveness, and inclusive opportunity across the County. The plan builds on existing County assets like talent and proximity to world-leading research institutions, while addressing emerging challenges and opportunities in the ecosystem and workforce development.

Smith also oversaw MCEDC’s rebrand, which included a refreshed logo, new website, and the launch of quarterly MCEDC-hosted events where each convened over 100 attendees. Smith has also prioritized building a best-in-class economic development team and has made several key hires, including a new Vice President of Business Development, Vice President of Economic Competitiveness, and Chief Operating Officer.

The Washington Business Journal’s Power 250 list also recognized several other Montgomery County leaders, including Co-founder of Xometry, Randy Altschuler, President and CEO of the Montgomery County Chamber of Commerce, Angela Franco, Founder & CEO of United Therapeutics, Dr. Martine Rothblatt, President & CEO of The Donohoe Companies, Christopher Bruch, and President of Montgomery College, Dr. Jermaine F. Williams.

“Dear PoPville,

Not too long after being bought out by corporate medicine, GW MFA pharmacy is shutting down entirely, giving only 2 weeks’ notice to their patients. They are doing practically nothing to assist patients with their prescriptions. Here is the email sent today to patients.”

“Dear MFA Community Member,

The GW MFA Pharmacy, located at 2150 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, is permanently closing. Our last day open will be Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and we will be permanently closed starting Wednesday, November 25, 2026. Until then, the Pharmacy’s new operating hours will be 8:30AM to 5:30PM, M-F, closed for lunch from 12:30PM to 1:30PM.

We are writing because our records show you have filled a prescription with us recently. After we close, your prescriptions will be transferred to Walgreens. You are free to choose any pharmacy you prefer instead, at no cost to you. Details on both options are below.

“New Coalition Warns Initiative 87’s $25 Mandate Would Drive Up Prices Across D.C., Calling It the Wrong Plan at the Worst Time”

By Prince Of Petworth
Published November 16, 2026 at 12:35PM

From a press release:

“A coalition of D.C. small businesses, nonprofits, workers, and community advocates is calling on voters to say No on 87, No on Higher Prices, in the District’s anticipated 2027 special election. Voters can learn more, sign up, and get involved at noi87.org.

Initiative 87 would require every employer in the District to pay a $25 minimum wage. It would also eliminate the separate base wage for tipped workers and ban sharing service changes with back-of-house employees. This would have a broad, negative impact on everyone from the corner cafes simply trying to survive, to the neighborhood child care centers who already face substantial financial challenges, to the nonprofits serving our most vulnerable. D.C.’s minimum wage is already $18.40 an hour, higher than any state, and it rises automatically with inflation every year.

“The cost of living is the defining challenge for District families right now, and Initiative 87 doesn’t solve the problem, it makes things worse,” said Anthony A. Williams, CEO and Executive Director of the Federal City Council and former Mayor of the District of Columbia. “When I came in as Chief Financial Officer, the District was climbing out of insolvency, and the most important work we did, in that office and then as Mayor, was restoring the faith and credit of the District.

“I know how hard-won that progress has been, and how quickly it can be lost,” Williams said. “With federal jobs leaving and household budgets already squeezed, Initiative 87 would show up in what families pay for everyday necessities. This is the time to steady the city’s footing, not to run an experiment no American city has tried.”
